checks.do: Which tab of the finding drawer holds the remediation guidance, and whether the page says it can include a workflow.
Which columns the Identity Findings list shows before reading a finding's severity, exploit ease or remediate ease.

purpose.statement: Identity Findings show identity-related security issues detected across connected identity providers and directories, which security teams can review and prioritize by severity.

quotes: Identity Findings provide visibility into identity-related security issues detected across connected identity providers and directories.
Security teams can review the security risks and prioritize remediation based on severity.

list-widgets.statement: The Identity Findings page (Identities > Identity Findings) has summary widgets, including Identity Findings Severity Over Time, a trend across Critical, High, Medium or Low, and Identity Findings Severity, the distribution by those levels.

quotes: On the Identity Findings page (Identities > Identity Findings), you can do the following:
Identity Findings Severity Over Time: Displays the trend of identity findings across severity levels (Critical, High, Medium, or Low) over a period of time.
Identity Findings Severity: Displays the distribution of identity findings by severity level (Critical, High, Medium, or Low).
View the summary of identity findings in the following widgets:

list-columns.statement: The identity findings list shows, for each finding, ID, Severity Score, Title, Tenant, Affected Entities, Vulnerability Exploit Ease, Techniques, Last Seen and Vulnerability Remediate Ease.

quotes: ID: The unique identifier for the identity finding.
Severity Score: The risk level of the finding based on the severity score.
Title: The title of the finding.
Tenant: The tenant where the finding was detected.
Affected Entities: The count and type of the impacted entities.
Vulnerability Exploit Ease: How easily an attacker can exploit the vulnerability based on required skills, conditions, and available tools.
Techniques: The relevant MITRE techniques associated with the risk.
Last Seen: When the finding was first and most recently detected.
Vulnerability Remediate Ease: How easily the vulnerability can be fixed based on required effort, changes, and potential impact on systems and operations.

list-actions.statement: The Identity Findings page can filter findings (for example by Title, Tenant Name and MITRE ATT&CK ID), group them (for example by Identity Finding ID, First Seen and Last Seen), export the list as a CSV file and include or exclude columns.

quotes: Filter identity findings based on different parameters (e.g., Title, Tenant Name, and MITRE ATT&CK ID).
Group the list of identity findings based on specific parameters (e.g., Identity Finding ID, Identity Finding First Seen, Identity Finding Last Seen).
Export the identity findings list as a CSV file.
Customize the identity findings list by including or excluding specific columns.

detail-contents.statement: Each identity finding includes contextual information such as the risk description, severity, affected tenants, MITRE ATT&CK mapping and recommended remediation steps, and its details open in a drawer when a finding is clicked on the Identity Findings page.

quotes: Each identity finding includes contextual information such as the risk description, severity, affected tenants, MITRE ATT&CK mapping, and recommended remediation steps.
On the Identity Findings page, click an identity finding to view its details.
The identity finding details drawer appears.

detail-fields.statement: The Details tab of the finding drawer typically includes Identity Finding, Last Seen, Tactics, Type of Risk, Techniques, Vulnerability Exploit Ease, Sub Techniques, Vulnerability Remediate Ease and Sources (the identity systems where the risk was detected, for example Active Directory or Entra ID).

quotes: This section typically includes:
Identity Finding: The name of the detected identity risk.
Tactics: The relevant MITRE tactic associated with the risk.
Type of Risk: The classification of the detected issue.
Sub Techniques: The relevant MITRE sub-techniques associated with the risk.
Sources: The identity systems where the risk was detected (e.g., Active Directory or Entra ID).
Vulnerability Exploit Ease: Indicates how easily an attacker can exploit the vulnerability based on required skills, conditions, and available tools.
Vulnerability Remediate Ease: Indicates how easily the vulnerability can be fixed based on required effort, changes, and potential impact on systems and operations.
The Details tab provides an overview of the identity risk and its security context
Last Seen: When the finding was first and most recently detected.
Techniques: The relevant MITRE techniques associated with the risk.

affected-tabs.statement: The finding drawer's Affected Identities tab lists all identities impacted by the finding, and its Affected Tenants tab lists all tenants or identity environments impacted by it; the page gives both tabs the same sentence about applying filters, downloading the list of tenants as a CSV file and customizing columns.

quotes: The Affected Identities tab lists all identities impacted by the finding.
You can also apply filters, download the list of tenants as a CSV file, or customize the columns displayed in the table.
evidence.after: The Affected Identities tab lists all identities impacted by the finding.

quotes: The Affected Tenants tab lists all tenants or identity environments impacted by the finding.
You can also apply filters, download the list of tenants as a CSV file, or customize the columns displayed in the table.
evidence.after: The Affected Tenants tab lists all tenants or identity environments impacted by the finding.

remediation-tab.statement: The Remediation tab gives recommended steps to resolve the finding; depending on the environment and configuration the guidance can include actions or a remediation workflow, and for each action the page says detailed information such as videos and scripts is available.

quotes: The Remediation tab provides recommended steps to resolve the detected issue.
Depending on the environment and configuration, the remediation guidance can include actions or a remediation workflow
For each action, you can view detailed information, including videos, script, etc. to accomplish the action.

remediation-workflow-actions.statement: The remediation workflow's possible actions include evaluating whether the configuration is required, implementing alternative security controls, removing insecure configurations, or applying appropriate mitigations.

quotes: The workflow guides you through possible actions, such as evaluating whether the configuration is required, implementing alternative security controls, removing insecure configurations, or applying appropriate mitigations.

safelist-from-remediation.statement: If a finding's configuration cannot be changed immediately, admins can choose to safelist the finding after evaluating the associated risk.

quotes: If the configuration cannot be changed immediately, admins can choose to safelist the finding after evaluating the associated risk.

admin-portal-relation.title: How the Identities menu findings relate to the ITDR Admin Portal pages
admin-portal-relation.detail: The captured Identity Findings pages describe the Identities > Identity Findings page and name the console 'Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform', while the Overview and Alerts pages name it 'Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal'; none says whether those are the same console, how the Identities menu relates to the legacy ITDR redirect and API parity questions recorded in identity-protection.overview (legacy-redirect, gap api-and-legacy-parity), or whether the page replaces, mirrors or sits beside the ITDR Admin Portal's Identity Posture, Change Detection and Risk Summary dashboards, or whether an identity finding is the same object as an ITDR 'Detailed Findings and Recommendations' item.

severity-and-ease.title: What score ranges give each severity level and what the exploit and remediate ease ratings mean
severity-and-ease.detail: The Identity Findings pages show a Severity Score and the levels Critical, High, Medium and Low but give no score ranges or calculation. Vulnerability Exploit Ease and Vulnerability Remediate Ease are described only as depending on required skills, conditions and tools, and on required effort, changes and impact; no thresholds are stated.

affected-identities-export.title: Whether the Affected Identities tab can export identities
affected-identities-export.detail: The Affected Identities tab text repeats the Affected Tenants wording 'download the list of tenants as a CSV file'; whether that tab exports identities is not stated.

safelist-location.title: Where an identity finding is safelisted
safelist-location.detail: The finding drawer says admins can choose to safelist the finding after evaluating the risk, but does not say where in the console this is done or how it relates to identity-protection.safelists. Roles and permissions needed to view or act on findings are also not stated.
